_doc: GENERATED by data/latex/gen-formulas.mjs from data/latex/100-formulas.md (the owner's library, verbatim), data/latex/pi-formulas.md (the pi category) and data/latex/plots.json (one plot spec per formula) - edit those, not this file. categories: [{id, label, includes?}] in the owner's order then pi (includes = ids of owner formulas that also list there); formulas: [{id (unique slug), number, title, category (a category id), latex (the display formula), description (one paragraph; inline math stays as $...$ for KaTeX auto-render), plot {caption, kind (function|illustration), vars [{symbol, label, default, min, max, step}], d2, d3 (layers of safe expressions, see plots.json), anim?, wave?}}]. The app adds a 'Mine' category from the user's saved formulas (build.json::latex.mine_category). test/test-calc-latex.sh --check fails if this file drifts from the sources.

categories.label: Fluid Dynamics, Chemistry, Cosmology & Nonlinear Systems

formulas.title: The Pythagorean Theorem
formulas.description: Defines the fundamental relationship between the sides of a right triangle in Euclidean geometry, serving as the basis for distance metrics, Euclidean vectors, and trigonometry.

plot.caption: Hypotenuse c = sqrt(a^2 + b^2): c against leg a for the chosen b (2D), and over both legs (3D).

formulas.title: Euler's Identity
formulas.description: Widely celebrated as one of the most beautiful equations in mathematics, it unifies the five fundamental constants ($e$, $i$, $\pi$, $1$, and $0$) using addition, multiplication, and exponentiation.

plot.caption: e^(i*theta) on the unit circle (2D) and as a helix (theta, cos, sin) (3D); at theta = pi the point is -1, so e^(i pi) + 1 = 0.

formulas.title: Euler's Formula
formulas.description: Establishes the fundamental bridge between trigonometric functions and complex exponential functions, underpinning signal processing and Fourier analysis.

plot.caption: Re and Im of e^(i k theta) = cos(k theta) + i sin(k theta) against theta (2D), and the helix (theta, cos, sin) (3D); k is the frequency.

formulas.title: The Quadratic Formula
formulas.description: Provides the exact analytical solution to the roots of any quadratic equation of the form $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$.

plot.caption: The parabola y = a x^2 + b x + c with its roots where it crosses 0 (2D), and the same polynomial over x and c (3D).

formulas.title: The Binomial Theorem
formulas.description: Describes the algebraic expansion of powers of a binomial sum into a series using binomial coefficients.

plot.caption: (x+y)^n against x, and its binomial expansion term by term (they coincide) (2D); (x+y)^n over x and y (3D).

formulas.title: Euler’s Polyhedral Formula
formulas.description: Relates the number of vertices ($V$), edges ($E$), and faces ($F$) of any convex polyhedron, forming the foundation of combinatorial topology.

plot.caption: Illustration: for the five regular polyhedra the point (V+F, E) lies on the line E = V+F-2 (2D); the chosen polyhedron drawn in 3D.

vars.label: Solid (1 tetra, 2 cube, 3 octa, 4 dodeca, 5 icosa)

formulas.title: The Law of Cosines
formulas.description: Generalizes the Pythagorean theorem to any arbitrary triangle, relating side lengths to the cosine of one of the angles.

plot.caption: Side c = sqrt(a^2+b^2-2ab cos C) against the angle C (2D), and over a and C (3D).

formulas.title: The Law of Sines
formulas.description: Relates the sides of an arbitrary triangle to the sines of their opposing angles and the radius $R$ of its circumscribed circle.

plot.caption: Side a = 2R sin A against the angle A for the circumradius R (2D), and over R and A (3D).

formulas.title: Heron's Formula
formulas.description: Calculates the area ($A$) of any triangle from its three side lengths ($a, b, c$), where $s = \frac{a+b+c}{2}$ is the semi-perimeter.

plot.caption: Triangle area A against side a (gaps where no triangle exists) (2D), and over a and b (3D).

formulas.title: The Prime Number Theorem
formulas.description: Describes the asymptotic distribution of prime numbers among positive integers, stating that the number of primes less than $x$ approaches $x/\ln x$ as $x \to \infty$.

plot.caption: The prime counting function pi(x) against x/ln x (2D); the curve (x, pi(x), x/ln x) (3D).

formulas.title: The Basel Problem (Euler's Sum)
formulas.description: Solved by Leonhard Euler in 1734, revealing an unexpected connection between reciprocal squares of integers and $\pi$.

plot.caption: Partial sums of 1/k^s with N terms against N, and the limit zeta(s) (2D); the term magnitude N^-s over N and s (3D).

formulas.title: The Riemann Zeta Function
formulas.description: Relates the summation over all integers to the Euler product over all prime numbers, central to modern analytic number theory.

plot.caption: zeta(s) from the sum over n and from the Euler product over primes up to N (2D); the partial sum over s and N (3D).

formulas.title: De Moivre’s Formula
formulas.description: Allows powers of complex numbers in polar form to be computed directly via angle multiplication.

plot.caption: Re and Im of (cos t + i sin t)^n = cos(nt) + i sin(nt) (2D); the helix (t, cos nt, sin nt) (3D); n is the frequency.

formulas.title: Stirling's Approximation
formulas.description: Provides an asymptotic estimate for factorials of large numbers, essential in combinatorics and statistical physics.

plot.caption: The ratio n! / (sqrt(2 pi n) (n/e)^n) tends to 1 (2D); the ratio with the 1/(12n) correction over n and m (3D).

formulas.title: The Chudnovsky Algorithm for $\pi$
formulas.description: An ultra-fast converging hypergeometric series used by modern supercomputers to compute trillions of digits of $\pi$.

plot.caption: Correct digits of pi after N terms of the Chudnovsky series (2D); the log10 term size over k and the constant b (3D).

formulas.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
formulas.description: Links differentiation and definite integration as inverse operations, enabling the analytical calculation of accumulated areas and quantities.

plot.caption: f(x) = x^3/6 - x with f'(x), and f(x) - f(a) = integral of f' from a to x; the bounds a and b marked (2D); f(b) - f(a) over a and b (3D).

formulas.title: The Formal Definition of the Derivative
formulas.description: Defines the instantaneous rate of change of a continuous function at a given point as the limit of a difference quotient.

plot.caption: The difference quotient of sin with step h against the true derivative cos (2D); the quotient over x and h (3D).

formulas.title: Integration by Parts
formulas.description: Derived from the product rule of differentiation, allowing the integration of products of functions.

plot.caption: With u = x, dv = cos(kx) dx: u*v, the integral of v du, and their difference, the integral of u dv (2D); the integral of u dv over x and k (3D).

formulas.title: Taylor Series Expansion
formulas.description: Represents any infinitely differentiable function as an infinite polynomial expansion evaluated around a reference point $a$.

plot.caption: sin x and its Taylor polynomial of degree N about 0 (2D); the error of the polynomial over x and N (3D).

formulas.title: The Continuous Fourier Transform
formulas.description: Decomposes a time-domain or spatial-domain function into its constituent frequency components.

plot.caption: A Gaussian f(x) of width s and its Fourier transform, which is a Gaussian of width 1/s (2D); the transform over xi and s (3D).

formulas.title: The Inverse Fourier Transform
formulas.description: Reconstructs the original time-domain function from its continuous frequency spectrum.

plot.caption: A Gaussian rebuilt from its spectrum cut off at band B, against the exact Gaussian (2D); the rebuilt function over x and B (3D).

formulas.title: The Laplace Transform
formulas.description: Transforms linear ordinary differential equations in the time domain into simpler algebraic equations in the complex frequency domain.

plot.caption: F(s) = 1/(s+a) for f(t) = e^(-at), and the same integral done numerically (2D); F over s and a (3D).

formulas.title: The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
formulas.description: A foundational inequality in linear algebra and functional analysis bounding the inner product of two vectors by their norms.

plot.caption: (u.v)^2 stays below |u|^2 |v|^2 as the angle between the vectors turns (2D); both sides over the angle and |v| (3D).

formulas.title: Cauchy's Integral Formula
formulas.description: Shows that for a holomorphic complex function, its value inside a closed contour is completely determined by values on the boundary.

plot.caption: Illustration: the contour circle and the point a inside it (2D); |1/(z-a)| over the complex plane, the pole at a (3D, clipped).

formulas.title: Cauchy's Residue Theorem
formulas.description: A powerful contour integration tool that evaluates complex line integrals by calculating local residues at interior singularities.

plot.caption: Illustration: the contour and two simple poles at +-p (2D); |1/((z-p)(z+p))| over the complex plane (3D, clipped).

formulas.title: The Divergence (Gauss-Ostrogradsky) Theorem
formulas.description: Relates the volume integral of the divergence of a vector field to the surface flux through its closed boundary.

plot.caption: Illustration: the field F = (x, k y) with the boundary circle of radius R (2D); the field F = (x, k y, z) as arrows in a cube (3D). Divergence is 1+k (2D).

formulas.title: Stokes' Theorem
formulas.description: Relates the surface integral of the curl of a vector field over an open surface to the circulation along the boundary curve.

plot.caption: Illustration: the rotating field F = k(-y, x) with a boundary loop of radius R (2D); the same field in 3D. Its curl is 2k.

formulas.title: Green’s Theorem
formulas.latex: \oint_C (L\,dx + M\,dy) = \iint_D \left(\frac{\partial M}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial L}{\partial y}\right) dA
formulas.description: A two-dimensional special case of Stokes' theorem relating line integrals around a plane curve to double integrals over the enclosed region.

plot.caption: Illustration: the field (L, M) = (-k y, x y) with a loop of radius R (2D); the integrand dM/dx - dL/dy = y + k over the plane (3D).

formulas.title: The Heat Equation
formulas.description: A parabolic partial differential equation governing the diffusion of thermal energy and passive particles over time.

plot.caption: The spreading Gaussian solution u(x,t) = exp(-x^2/(4at)) / sqrt(4 pi a t) at time t, with an earlier snapshot (2D); the space-time surface (3D).

formulas.title: The Classical Wave Equation
formulas.description: A hyperbolic partial differential equation describing the propagation of mechanical, acoustic, and electromagnetic waves through a medium at speed $v$.

plot.caption: A travelling wave u = A sin(2 pi f (x/v - t) + phase) at time t (2D); the space-time surface (3D). Change the frequency f.

formulas.title: Bayes' Theorem
formulas.description: Calculates conditional probability by updating the prior belief $P(A)$ in light of observed evidence $B$.

plot.caption: The posterior P(A|B) against the prior P(A), with the prior itself dashed (2D); the posterior over the prior and the false positive rate (3D).

formulas.title: The Normal (Gaussian) Distribution
formulas.description: Defines the symmetric bell-shaped probability density function with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$.

plot.caption: The normal density and its cumulative distribution (2D); the density over x and the spread (3D).

formulas.title: The Central Limit Theorem
formulas.description: States that the normalized sum of independent and identically distributed random variables tends toward a standard normal distribution.

plot.caption: The density of the standardised mean of n uniform variables (Irwin-Hall) against the standard normal (2D); that density over z and n (3D).

formulas.title: The Poisson Distribution
formulas.description: Models the probability of $k$ independent events occurring within a fixed interval given a known average rate $\lambda$.

plot.caption: The Poisson probabilities P(X = k) as stems for the rate lambda (2D); the probability over k and lambda (3D).

formulas.title: The Binomial Distribution
formulas.description: Calculates the probability of observing exactly $k$ successes out of $n$ independent Bernoulli trials with probability $p$.

plot.caption: The binomial probabilities P(X = k) as stems for n trials and success rate p (2D); the probability over k and p (3D).

formulas.title: Variance of a Random Variable
formulas.description: Measures the dispersion or spread of values of a random variable around its mathematical expectation $\mu$.

plot.caption: Var(X) = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2 for a binomial count, from the two sides (identical) against p (2D); the variance over p and n (3D).

formulas.title: Covariance
formulas.description: Quantifies the joint directional variability of two distinct random variables.

plot.caption: A cloud of 300 correlated pairs with covariance rho*s1*s2 (2D); their joint density over the plane (3D).

formulas.title: Pearson Correlation Coefficient
formulas.description: Measures the strength and direction of linear association between two variables, normalized between $-1$ and $+1$.

plot.caption: The same cloud with its regression line y = rho*(s2/s1)*x (2D); the joint density for sigma_x, sigma_y and rho (3D).

formulas.title: Shannon Entropy
formulas.description: Quantifies the fundamental limit of expected information content, uncertainty, and lossless compression rate for a discrete source.

plot.caption: Binary entropy H(p) in bits (2D); the entropy of a three-outcome distribution (p1, p2, 1-p1-p2) (3D).

formulas.title: Kullback-Leibler Divergence
formulas.description: Measures the relative statistical distance and information loss when approximating true distribution $P$ with reference distribution $Q$.

plot.caption: D(P||Q) and D(Q||P) for Bernoulli P (p) and Q (q) against q: not symmetric (2D); D(P||Q) over p and q (3D).

formulas.title: Chebyshev's Inequality
formulas.description: Guarantees an upper bound on the probability that a random variable deviates by more than $k$ standard deviations from the mean.

plot.caption: The bound 1/k^2 against the true tail of a normal and of a Laplace variable (2D); the slack of the bound over k and the mix m (3D).

formulas.title: Weak Law of Large Numbers
formulas.description: States that the sample average of independent trials converges in probability toward the theoretical population mean $\mu$.

plot.caption: Running mean of n deterministic pseudo-random coin flips (rate p) settling at p (2D); the distance |mean - p| over n and the seed (3D).

formulas.title: The Black-Scholes Equation
formulas.latex: \frac{\partial V}{\partial t} + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 S^2 \frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial S^2} + rS \frac{\partial V}{\partial S} - rV = 0
formulas.description: A partial differential equation modeling the fair financial pricing of European derivative options over time.

plot.caption: European call value from the Black-Scholes solution against the price S, with the payoff (2D); the value over S and the time to expiry (3D).

formulas.title: Newton's Second Law of Motion
formulas.description: Relates net applied force ($\mathbf{F}$) to the time rate of change of linear momentum ($\mathbf{p}$), or mass times acceleration for invariant mass.

plot.caption: F = m a against the acceleration, and the momentum gained after t seconds (2D); F over m and a (3D).

formulas.title: Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation
formulas.description: Describes the inverse-square gravitational attraction between two point masses separated by distance $r$.

plot.caption: Attraction F = G m1 m2 / r^2 against the distance r (masses in 1e24 kg, r in 1e8 m, force in 1e18 N at the default scale) (2D); F over r and m1 (3D).

formulas.title: Kinetic Energy
formulas.description: Quantifies the mechanical work stored in an object of mass $m$ by virtue of its velocity $v$ or momentum $p$.

plot.caption: E = m v^2 / 2 against the speed, and p^2/(2m) from the momentum (identical) (2D); E over v and m (3D).

formulas.title: Gravitational Potential Energy (Uniform Field)
formulas.description: Measures potential energy gained by lifting mass $m$ to height $h$ in a uniform gravitational field $g$.

plot.caption: U = m g h against the height for the field g (2D); U over h and g (3D, from the Moon to Jupiter).

formulas.title: General Gravitational Potential Energy
formulas.description: Describes the potential energy of a two-body system separated by distance $r$, set to zero at infinite separation.

plot.caption: U(r) = -G M m / r against the distance (M in 1e24 kg, r in 1e6 m, U in MJ) (2D); U over r and M (3D).

formulas.title: Hooke's Law
formulas.description: Models linear restoring force exerted by an ideal spring stretched or compressed by displacement $x$.

plot.caption: Spring force F = -k x and its stored energy k x^2 / 2 against the extension (2D); F over x and k (3D).

formulas.title: Simple Harmonic Angular Frequency
formulas.description: Defines the natural angular frequency of oscillation for an undamped mass-spring oscillator.

plot.caption: The oscillation x(t) = A cos(omega t) with omega = sqrt(k/m) (2D); omega over k and m (3D). Change the stiffness to change the frequency.

formulas.title: Period of a Simple Pendulum
formulas.description: Approximates the small-amplitude period of oscillation for a pendulum of length $L$ in gravitational field $g$.

plot.caption: Period T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) against the length L, with the large-angle correction (2D); T over L and g (3D).

formulas.title: Kepler's Third Law (Harmonic Law)
formulas.description: Relates orbital period ($T$) squared to semi-major axis ($a$) cubed for elliptical orbits around a central mass.

plot.caption: Orbital period T = sqrt(a^3 / M) in years against the semi-major axis (AU) around a star of M suns, with the planets for M = 1 (2D); T over a and M (3D).

formulas.title: The Work-Energy Theorem
formulas.description: Demonstrates that the net work done by all forces on a body equals the net change in its kinetic energy.

plot.caption: Force F(x) = F0 + c x and the work W(x) = F0 x + c x^2 / 2, which is the kinetic energy gained (2D); W over x and c (3D).

formulas.title: The Euler-Lagrange Equation
formulas.description: Forms the cornerstone of analytical Lagrangian mechanics, identifying paths of stationary action for generalized coordinates $q_i$.

plot.caption: The path q(t) = A cos(omega t + phase) that satisfies the Euler-Lagrange equation for L = m qdot^2/2 - k q^2/2, with qdot (2D); the curve (t, q, qdot) (3D).

formulas.title: Hamilton's Canonical Equations
formulas.description: Replaces second-order Lagrangian equations with a coupled set of first-order differential equations in phase space $(q, p)$.

plot.caption: Pendulum phase plane: the flow field (q̇, ṗ) with the level curve of H = p^2/2m - m gl cos q for energy E (2D); H over q and p (3D).

formulas.title: The First Law of Thermodynamics
formulas.description: Expresses conservation of energy: internal energy change ($dU$) equals heat added ($\delta Q$) minus thermodynamic work done ($\delta W$).

plot.caption: Ideal-gas P-V diagram: the isotherm (heat in = work out) and the adiabat (no heat) from the same start (2D); P over V and T (3D).

formulas.title: The Second Law of Thermodynamics (Clausius Inequality)
formulas.description: States that the entropy ($S$) of an isolated physical system never decreases over time during spontaneous processes.

plot.caption: Entropy created by moving heat Q from a hot body to a cold one, Q (1/Tc - 1/Th), against Tc: negative when the direction is forbidden (2D); over Tc and Th (3D).

formulas.title: Boltzmann’s Entropy Formula
formulas.description: Bridges microscopic states and macroscopic thermodynamics, connecting thermodynamic entropy to the number of microstates $\Omega$.

plot.caption: S/k = ln(Omega) for N two-state particles with a fraction f up, Omega = C(N, fN) (2D); S/k over f and N (3D).

formulas.title: The Ideal Gas Law
formulas.description: Equation of state describing an idealized non-interacting gas in terms of pressure, volume, temperature, and substance quantity.

plot.caption: Pressure P = n R T / V against the volume at T and at 2T (2D); P over V and T (3D). P in kPa, V in litres.

formulas.title: Carnot Engine Thermal Efficiency
formulas.description: Sets the theoretical maximum reversible thermodynamic efficiency for any heat engine operating between hot ($T_H$) and cold ($T_C$) reservoirs.

plot.caption: Efficiency 1 - Tc/Th against Tc, below zero where Tc exceeds Th (2D); over Tc and Th (3D).

formulas.title: Maxwell-Boltzmann Speed Distribution
formulas.description: Gives the statistical probability density of molecular speeds for an ideal gas at thermodynamic temperature $T$.

plot.caption: Speed distribution f(v) of a gas of molar mass M (g/mol) at temperature T (2D); f over v and T (3D).

formulas.title: Gibbs Free Energy
formulas.description: Thermodynamic potential used to predict chemical reaction spontaneity and equilibrium at constant temperature and pressure.

plot.caption: dG = dH - T dS against T: the reaction is spontaneous where it is below 0 (2D); dG over T and dS (3D). kJ and kJ/K.

formulas.title: Enthalpy Definition
formulas.description: Quantifies the total heat content of a thermodynamic system, incorporating internal energy ($U$) and flow work ($PV$).

plot.caption: H = U + P V against the volume at fixed U and P (2D); H over V and P (3D). kPa and litres give joules.

formulas.title: The Stefan-Boltzmann Law
formulas.description: States that total radiant energy emitted per unit surface area of a blackbody is proportional to the fourth power of absolute temperature.

plot.caption: Radiated power per area j = eps sigma T^4 against T (2D); j over T and the emissivity (3D). W/m^2.

formulas.title: Planck’s Law of Blackbody Radiation
formulas.description: Accurately predicts spectral radiation density without the classical ultraviolet catastrophe, initiating quantum mechanics.

plot.caption: Spectral radiance of a black body against the wavelength (micrometres) at temperature T (2D); over wavelength and T (3D).

formulas.title: Gauss's Law (Electrostatics)
formulas.description: States that the divergence of the electric field equals local volume charge density divided by vacuum permittivity.

plot.caption: Field of a point charge q: arrows pointing out of a positive charge, in to a negative one (2D); the field in a cube (3D).

formulas.title: Gauss's Law for Magnetism
formulas.description: Expresses the non-existence of isolated magnetic monopoles; magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops.

plot.caption: Field of a magnetic dipole in the x-z plane: the lines close on themselves (2D); the dipole field in a cube (3D).

formulas.title: Faraday’s Law of Electromagnetic Induction
formulas.description: States that a time-varying magnetic field induces a spatially circulating non-conservative electric field.

plot.caption: Induced electric field circulating around a changing uniform magnetic field of radius R (2D); the field in a cube (3D).

formulas.title: The Ampère-Maxwell Law
formulas.description: Shows that magnetic fields are produced by conduction current densities ($\mathbf{J}$) and Maxwell's displacement currents.

plot.caption: Magnetic field circling a wire carrying current I (2D); the field around the wire in a cube (3D).

formulas.title: The Lorentz Force Law
formulas.description: Calculates the total electromagnetic force acting on a particle carrying electric charge $q$ moving with velocity $\mathbf{v}$.

plot.caption: Path of a charge in crossed fields E and B, a cycloid in the plane (2D) with the drift along B in 3D. w is the cyclotron frequency.

formulas.title: Coulomb’s Law
formulas.description: Quantifies the electrostatic force between two stationary electric point charges separated by distance $r$.

plot.caption: Force F = k q1 q2 / r^2 against the distance (charges in µC, r in cm, F in N; negative = attraction) (2D); F over r and q1 (3D).

formulas.title: Ohm's Law (Microscopic and Macroscopic)
formulas.description: Relates electric potential difference ($V$) across a conductor to current ($I$) and electrical resistance ($R$).

plot.caption: V = I R against the current for resistance R, and for 2R (2D); V over I and R (3D). The microscopic J = sigma E is the same line.

formulas.title: Snell’s Law of Refraction
formulas.description: Describes the angular bending of light rays passing across the interface between two media of differing refractive indices.

plot.caption: Refraction angle against the incidence angle; the curve stops at the critical angle where light is totally reflected (2D); the angle over theta1 and n2 (3D).

formulas.title: The Poynting Vector
formulas.description: Represents the directional energy flux density (power per unit area) transported by an electromagnetic wave.

plot.caption: A plane wave: E, B and the energy flow S = E B at time t (2D); S over position and time (3D). Change the frequency f.

formulas.title: Speed of Light from Electromagnetic Constants
formulas.description: Directly proves that light is an electromagnetic wave whose speed is fixed by electric permittivity and magnetic permeability.

plot.caption: Speed of light 1/sqrt(eps mu) in a medium, in 1e8 m/s, against the relative permittivity (2D); over eps_r and mu_r (3D).

formulas.title: Mass-Energy Equivalence
formulas.description: Asserts that mass and rest energy are directly proportional and interchangeable via the speed of light squared.

plot.caption: E = m c^2 in units of 1e16 J against the mass in kg (2D); E over the mass and a scale of c (3D).

vars.label: c as a fraction of its value

formulas.title: Relativistic Energy-Momentum Relation
formulas.description: Calculates total relativistic energy ($E$) for particles with rest mass $m_0$ and momentum $p$, including massless photons ($E = pc$).

plot.caption: Total energy sqrt((pc)^2 + (mc^2)^2) in MeV against pc, with the massless line and the kinetic energy (2D); E over pc and mc^2 (3D).

formulas.title: The Lorentz Factor
formulas.description: Dimensionless scale factor by which time, length, and relativistic mass scale as relative speed $v$ approaches $c$.

plot.caption: gamma against v/c, rising without bound near 1 (2D); gamma over the velocity components (bx, by) inside the unit disc (3D).

formulas.title: Relativistic Time Dilation
formulas.description: Shows that a clock moving at speed $v$ ticks slower relative to a stationary observer's reference frame.

plot.caption: Time between two ticks seen by an observer: dt/sqrt(1-b^2) against v/c (2D); over v/c and the proper time (3D).

formulas.title: Relativistic Length Contraction
formulas.description: Demonstrates that the physical length of an object appears contracted along its direction of travel at relativistic speeds.

plot.caption: Length L0 sqrt(1-b^2) seen by an observer against v/c (2D); over v/c and the rest length (3D).

formulas.title: Einstein's Field Equations of General Relativity
formulas.description: Relates the geometry and curvature of spacetime ($G_{\mu\nu}$) to the distribution of matter and energy ($T_{\mu\nu}$).

plot.caption: Illustration: the time-time metric -(1 - rs/r) of a mass against r (2D); the embedding surface (Flamm paraboloid) of the space around it (3D).

formulas.title: The Schwarzschild Radius
formulas.description: Calculates the radius defining the event horizon of a non-rotating spherically symmetric black hole of mass $M$.

plot.caption: rs = 2GM/c^2 in km against the mass in suns (2D); the horizon sphere of the chosen mass (3D).

formulas.title: The Spacetime Invariant Interval
formulas.description: Defines the invariant distance between two events in flat Minkowski spacetime, invariant across all inertial reference frames.

plot.caption: Illustration: the light cone and the curves of constant interval s2 in an x-ct diagram (2D); the interval x^2 + y^2 - (ct)^2 over the plane (3D).

formulas.title: The Planck-Einstein Relation
formulas.description: States that the energy of a photon is directly quantized in discrete packets proportional to its electromagnetic frequency.

plot.caption: Photon energy E = h nu in eV against the frequency in THz (2D); the energy of N photons over nu and N (3D).

formulas.title: The de Broglie Wavelength
formulas.description: Establishes wave-particle duality, showing that every moving physical particle with momentum $p$ possesses a characteristic wavelength.

plot.caption: Wavelength lambda = h/(m v) in nm against the speed (1e6 m/s) for a particle of m electron masses (2D); over v and m (3D).

formulas.title: The Time-Dependent Schrödinger Equation
formulas.description: Governs the deterministic evolution of the quantum wave function $\Psi$ over time under Hamiltonian operator $\hat{H}$.

plot.caption: A free Gaussian wave packet: density |psi|^2 spreading and moving, with an illustrative Re psi (2D); the density over x and t (3D). hbar = m = 1.

formulas.title: The Time-Independent Schrödinger Equation
formulas.description: An eigenvalue problem determining stationary quantum energy states ($E$) and spatial wavefunctions ($\psi$).

plot.caption: Particle in a box of width L: the eigenfunction psi_n and its density, with E_n = n^2 pi^2/(2L^2) (2D); psi over x and n (3D).

formulas.title: Heisenberg’s Uncertainty Principle
formulas.description: Sets the fundamental quantum mechanical bound on the simultaneous measurement precision of position and momentum.

plot.caption: The smallest allowed sigma_p = hbar/(2 sigma_x) and that of the oscillator level n against sigma_x (2D); sigma_x sigma_p - hbar/2 over both (3D). hbar = 1.

formulas.title: The Dirac Equation
formulas.description: Unifies quantum mechanics with special relativity for spin-$1/2$ fermions, predicting antimatter and intrinsic spin.

plot.caption: The relativistic dispersion E = +-sqrt(p^2 + m^2) with the gap 2m (2D); both energy sheets over (px, py) (3D). c = 1.

formulas.title: Bohr Orbit Radius
formulas.description: Calculates the quantized radius of stable electron orbits in hydrogen-like atoms for principal quantum number $n$.

plot.caption: Bohr radii r_n = a0 n^2 / Z (nm) as stems (2D); the first four orbits drawn as circles (3D).

formulas.title: The Rydberg Formula
formulas.description: Predicts wavelengths of spectral emission lines caused by electron transitions between discrete energy shells in hydrogen.

plot.caption: Spectral line wavelengths (nm) for the lower level n1 as n2 grows (2D); wavelength over n1 and n2 (3D).

formulas.title: The Fermi-Dirac Distribution
formulas.description: Describes statistical energy level occupation for identical fermions obeying the Pauli exclusion principle.

plot.caption: Occupation 1/(exp((en-mu)/kT)+1) against the energy, with the zero-temperature step (2D); occupation over e and kT (3D).

formulas.title: The Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations
formulas.description: Governs the momentum conservation and fluid motion for viscous, incompressible Newtonian fluid flows.

plot.caption: The Taylor-Green vortex, an exact solution, decaying with viscosity nu: velocity arrows at time t (2D); its vorticity surface (3D).

formulas.title: The Fluid Continuity Equation
formulas.description: Expresses the local conservation of mass within a continuous fluid or compressible medium.

plot.caption: A density pulse carried along by a flow u: rho(x,t) = rho0(x - u t) (2D); the pulse in space-time (3D).

formulas.title: Bernoulli's Principle
formulas.description: Expresses conservation of mechanical energy along a streamline for steady, frictionless, incompressible fluid flow.

plot.caption: Pressure p2 (kPa) in a pipe whose cross-section changes by the ratio a = A2/A1 (2D); p2 over a and the inflow speed (3D).

formulas.title: The Arrhenius Equation
formulas.description: Models the temperature dependence of chemical reaction rate constants based on activation energy $E_a$.

plot.caption: Rate constant k = A exp(-Ea/RT) against T (2D); k over T and Ea (3D). Ea in kJ/mol.

formulas.title: The Nernst Equation
formulas.description: Determines the equilibrium reduction potential of an electrochemical cell as a function of temperature and reaction quotient $Q$.

plot.caption: Cell potential E = E0 - (RT/zF) ln Q against log10 Q (2D); E over log10 Q and the temperature (3D).

formulas.title: The Hubble-Lemaître Law
formulas.description: Describes the cosmological expansion of the universe, relating recessional velocity ($v$) of galaxies to physical distance ($d$).

plot.caption: Recession speed v = H0 d against the distance (Mpc), with the two measured H0 values dashed (2D); v over d and H0 (3D). km/s.

formulas.title: The First Friedmann Equation
formulas.description: Derives the expansion rate of homogeneous, isotropic universes from general relativity, where $a(t)$ is the scale factor.

plot.caption: Expansion rate H(a)/H0 = sqrt(Om a^-3 + Ok a^-2 + OL) against the scale factor (2D); over a and Om (3D). Ok = 1 - Om - OL.

formulas.title: The Logistic Map
formulas.description: A canonical nonlinear polynomial mapping exhibiting period-doubling routes to deterministic chaos in dynamic systems.

plot.caption: The bifurcation diagram: late iterates of x -> r x (1-x) for each r (2D); the iterate x_n over r and the step n (3D).

formulas.title: Leibniz series
formulas.description: The alternating sum of the odd reciprocals, found by Madhava and Leibniz; it is $\arctan 1$ and converges very slowly, gaining about one digit per tenfold increase in terms.

plot.caption: Partial sums of the Leibniz series 4(1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - ...) closing in on pi (2D); the Gregory partial sum over N and the argument z, z = 1 being Leibniz (3D).

formulas.title: Nilakantha series
formulas.description: A 15th-century series that starts from 3 and adds alternating cubic-denominator corrections; far faster than Leibniz.

plot.caption: Partial sums of 3 + 4/(2·3·4) - 4/(4·5·6) + ... (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

formulas.title: Wallis product
formulas.description: John Wallis's 1656 infinite product, the first exact expression for $\pi$ as a limit of rational numbers.

plot.caption: Partial Wallis products 2·Π 4k^2/(4k^2-1) rising to pi (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

formulas.title: Viète's formula
formulas.description: The first infinite expression for $\pi$ (1593), built from nested square roots; each factor is $\cos(\pi/2^{k+1})$, the polygon-doubling of Archimedes.

plot.caption: Viete's product: pi = 2 / Π cos(pi/2^(k+1)), the nested radicals, after N factors (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

formulas.title: Machin's formula
formulas.description: John Machin's 1706 identity; two rapidly converging arctangent series computed $\pi$ to 100 digits and remained the workhorse for two centuries.

plot.caption: Machin: 16 arctan(1/5) - 4 arctan(1/239) with N series terms each (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

formulas.title: Bailey–Borwein–Plouffe formula
formulas.description: The 1995 spigot formula that yields the $n$-th hexadecimal digit of $\pi$ without computing the earlier ones.

plot.caption: BBP: pi = Σ 16^-k (4/(8k+1) - 2/(8k+4) - 1/(8k+5) - 1/(8k+6)) after N terms (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

formulas.title: Ramanujan's 1914 series
formulas.description: Srinivasa Ramanujan's rapidly convergent series; every term adds about eight correct digits, and it is the ancestor of the Chudnovsky algorithm.

plot.caption: Ramanujan's 1914 series: each term adds about 8 digits (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

formulas.title: Gauss–Legendre algorithm
formulas.latex: a_{n+1} = \frac{a_n + b_n}{2},\quad b_{n+1} = \sqrt{a_n b_n},\quad \pi \approx \frac{4\,a_N^2}{1 - \sum_{j=1}^{N} 2^{j+1}\left(a_j^2 - b_j^2\right)},\quad a_0 = 1,\ b_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
formulas.description: An iteration built on the arithmetic–geometric mean: the number of correct digits doubles at every step, so four steps give more than 19 digits.

plot.caption: Gauss-Legendre: the digits double with every AGM step; N steps (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

formulas.title: Euler's ζ(4)
formulas.description: Euler's evaluation of the zeta function at 4, giving $\pi = \left(90\,\zeta(4)\right)^{1/4}$; it converges much faster than the Basel sum (#11).

plot.caption: pi estimated as (90 Σ 1/k^4)^(1/4) after N terms (2D); the term size 1/k^s over N and s (3D).

formulas.title: The Gaussian integral
formulas.description: The area under the bell curve; it follows from the polar-coordinate trick $\iint e^{-(x^2+y^2)}\,dx\,dy = \pi$ and underlies the normal distribution.

plot.caption: The Gaussian e^(-x^2) and the area -x..x under it, sqrt(pi) erf(x), approaching sqrt(pi) (2D); the surface e^(-(x^2+y^2)) whose volume is pi (3D).

formulas.title: Area of a circle
formulas.description: The area enclosed by a circle of radius $r$; Archimedes squeezed it between inscribed and circumscribed polygons.

plot.caption: Area of the circle pi r^2 against r, with the area of an inscribed n-gon (2D); the n-gon area over r and n approaching pi r^2 (3D).

formulas.title: Circumference of a circle
formulas.description: The definition of $\pi$ as the ratio of the circumference to the diameter, $\pi = C/d$.

plot.caption: Circumference 2 pi r against r, with the perimeter of an inscribed n-gon (2D); the perimeter over r and n (3D).

formulas.title: Buffon's needle
formulas.description: The probability that a needle of length $\ell$ dropped on lines spaced $t$ apart crosses one; counting crossings estimates $\pi$.

plot.caption: Buffon: pi estimated as 2 l n / (t hits) from n pseudo-random needle drops (2D); the drops as points (distance, angle, hit) (3D).

formulas.title: Monte Carlo estimate of π
formulas.description: Random points in the unit square fall inside the quarter circle with probability $\pi/4$; the error shrinks like $1/\sqrt{N}$.

plot.caption: Random points in the unit square: those inside the quarter circle (above) and outside, pi ~ 4 inside/total (2D); random points in a cube, the octant of the ball holds pi/6 of them (3D).

formulas.title: Stirling's √(2π)
formulas.description: The constant in Stirling's approximation, proved by combining Wallis's product with the Gaussian integral.

plot.caption: n! / (sqrt(n) (n/e)^n) tends to sqrt(2 pi) (2D); the same ratio with the 1/(12n) correction over n and m (3D).

formulas.title: Gregory's arctangent series
formulas.description: James Gregory's power series for the inverse tangent; at $x = 1$ it gives the Leibniz series and for small $x$ it is the engine of Machin-type formulas.

plot.caption: arctan x and its Gregory partial sum of N terms, with 4 arctan(1) = pi at x = 1 (2D); the partial-sum error over x and N (3D).

formulas.title: Newton–Euler arcsine series
formulas.description: Newton's series for the inverse sine; putting $x = 1/2$ gives $\pi/6$ with a geometric rate of convergence.

plot.caption: arcsin x and its series partial sum of N terms, with 6 arcsin(1/2) = pi (2D); the partial sum over x and N (3D).

formulas.title: Lambert's continued fraction
formulas.description: The continued fraction with which Lambert proved in 1761 that $\pi$ is irrational: for rational $x \ne 0$ the value cannot be rational, yet $\tan(\pi/4) = 1$.

plot.caption: Lambert's continued fraction for tan x cut at depth N against tan x (2D); its error over x and the depth (3D).

formulas.title: Ramanujan–Sato series
formulas.description: One of Ramanujan's series for $1/\pi$ that Sato's theory explains: rational terms built on the central binomial coefficients, each adding almost two correct digits.

plot.caption: A Ramanujan-Sato series, 16/pi = Σ (42k+5) C(2k,k)^3 / 2^(12k), after N terms: each term adds almost two digits (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

formulas.title: Euler's arctangent identity
formulas.description: A special case of $\arctan a + \arctan\frac{1-a}{1+a} = \frac{\pi}{4}$, the kind of identity from which Machin-like formulas are built.

plot.caption: arctan a + arctan((1-a)/(1+a)) = pi/4 for every a: the two parts and their constant sum (2D); arctan x + arctan y with the line where the sum is pi/4 (3D).

formulas.title: Euler's sine product
formulas.description: Euler's factorisation of the sine over its zeros; comparing coefficients gives the Basel sum and, at $x = 1/2$, Wallis's product.

plot.caption: sin(pi x) and Euler's product pi x Π (1 - x^2/n^2) over n <= N (2D); the product over x and N (3D).

formulas.title: Γ(1/2) = √π
formulas.description: The value of the gamma function at one half, equivalent to the Gaussian integral and the root of the $\pi$ in many probability and physics formulas.

plot.caption: The gamma function with Gamma(1/2) = sqrt(pi) marked (2D); the beta function B(x, y) with B(1/2, 1/2) = pi (3D).

formulas.title: Euler's reflection formula
formulas.description: Links the gamma function at $z$ and $1-z$ to $\pi$; at $z = 1/2$ it gives $\Gamma(1/2)^2 = \pi$.

plot.caption: Gamma(z) Gamma(1-z) against pi / sin(pi z): the same curve (2D); the product times sin(pi y) over z and y, equal to pi along y = z (3D).

formulas.title: Archimedes' polygon bounds
formulas.description: Half the perimeter of the inscribed and circumscribed regular $n$-gons brackets $\pi$; Archimedes used $n = 96$ to show $223/71 < \pi < 22/7$.

plot.caption: Archimedes: for an n-gon the inscribed n sin(pi/n) and circumscribed n tan(pi/n) half-perimeters bracket pi (2D); the bracket width over n (3D).

formulas.title: Madhava's series
formulas.description: Madhava of Sangamagrama's 14th-century series from $\arctan(1/\sqrt{3}) = \pi/6$; the ratio $-1/3$ makes it converge geometrically.

plot.caption: Madhava: pi = sqrt(12) Σ (-1/3)^k / (2k+1) after N terms (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).
